title: Number each item in a list
prompt:
You have an array of item names. For each item, build an object with two fields: `position` (starting from 1, not 0) and `item`.

Keep the original order.
hints: `map` gives you access to two things at once: the element (`$`) and its index (`$$`). You need both.
The index is zero-based, but the task asks for one-based positions. So index 0 becomes position 1, index 1 becomes position 2, and so on.
Inside your map, return an object with `position: $$ + 1` (to adjust from zero-based to one-based) and `item: $` (the element itself).

mustFail.why: forgets to adjust the index from zero-based to one-based

explanation.approach: When you map over an array, you have access to the current element (via `$`) and its position in the array (via `$$`). The position is zero-based by default, so you add 1 to get a human-friendly one-based count. Build an object with both pieces of information.

snippets.label: The answer
snippets.note: `$` is the element, `$$` is the index. Index 0 becomes position 1, index 1 becomes position 2, and so on.

snippets.label: What $$ actually is
snippets.note: `$$` is zero-based. The first element is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on.

snippets.label: The zero-based mistake
snippets.note: Forgetting to add 1 gives you zero-based positions. It is valid DataWeave, but it does not answer the task.

snippets.label: What happens if you only use $ without the index
snippets.note: You lose the position information entirely. `map` does not automatically include it; you have to ask for it with `$$`.

snippets.label: The long form with named parameters
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map ((element, index) -> {position: index + 1, item: element})
snippets.note: Instead of `$` and `$$`, you can name your parameters. The second parameter is the index, the first is the element. Identical result.
